entry.title: The 118 - Bottled Up
entry.summary:
Author: Deathorcake

Rating: Not RatedLanguage: EnglishWords: 9,513Chapters: 7/7Kudos: 13

Summary: Chimney didn’t think he’d ever get used to calling it ‘his office’, even though it had been a few months already since he’d stepped into the impossibly large captain’s shoes. As he passed by the plaque fixed on the wall just outside the office door, he reached up and touched the cold metal right next to where the name was etched and bowed his head in a nod of respect to his predecessor, as he had at the start of every shift since it had been screwed into place. He wondered, if he kept doing this every day, how long it would take that spot to begin to change colour. And whether it would take equally as long for these feelings to fade. Or would it remain this way for the decades it would take to wear it down the metal to reveal the wooden mount underneath. Or During a freakishly quiet shift, the 118 have no choice but to face each other and the personal demons that threaten to tear the fire family apart in the aftermath of the loss of their beloved Bobby Nash.

Summary: Buck finds a particularly cute photo of Chris holding a baby goat, which he’s not sure Eddie has, and that is a crime. Buck needs Eddie to see this image right this second and have it in his camera roll forever. “Eddie, touch tips?” he says mindlessly. Tapping on the share icon and opening Airdrop. No matter how much Eddie complains about technology, even he has to admit that Airdrop is a godsend function. You just have to tap the front of your phones together, and a cute photo of Chris appears. Who wouldn’t appreciate that? Eddie chokes on his drink and splutters for a moment. Buck finds it kinda cute that even at 34 years old, Eddie can’t manage to take a simple sip. “Right now?” Eddie asks after he calms down. “Yes, right now!” Buck hurries him along. He holds his phone to the side where Eddie is sitting, but no tap comes. Buck gazes up from his spot, and what he lands on is a sight for sore eyes. Or maybe the vision makes his eyes sore. He’s not really sure. “Eddie, where the fuck are your pants?” Buck asks in a tight voice.
